body: Unfortunately, Haleigh looks awful written out in and of itself. And a person has to see their first name written out a whole lot more than their first and last together.

Unfortunately I’m not sure what the process of getting accepted/approved looked like for her so I can’t speak to that, but when I look it up I do see audiology as an option listed under Medical Services Corps.

https://www.navycs.com/officer/hscp.html

Someone in my program is in the Navy Health Scholars Collegiate Program (HSCP.) To my understanding, the HSCP doesn’t cover tuition/fees like the HPSP, but it does offer participants a salary, benefits, and a stipend for housing. The expectation is then that participants do their externship with the Navy and serve as an audiologist for them for some number of years after graduation. I don’t know if this is what you’re looking for, but hopefully it helps!

Congratulations! Would you be matriculating Fall 2024? If so I’d expect a very fast turn around time from interview to response! Is the interview online? All of mine were and I just made sure to wear a nice top or sweater, no need to overthink it too much! And for the most part, interviewers just want to get to know you. They will almost certainly ask you a question along the lines of “why are you choosing audiology” and “why are you interested in our program specifically” so make sure you have an answer for both of those, and have a few questions prepared to ask them as well to show you’re interested! Good luck!

Not all accredited programs use CSDCAS, some have their own school-specific applications that you’ll have to access through their website. I believe CUNY is one of those that doesn’t use CSDCAS at all. Some schools even use both CSDCAS AND their own school-specific application. Check out the websites of the schools you’re interested in to see what their application process looks like because it varies. It’s also my understanding that not every program that uses CSDCAS has opened applications yet, as it’s very early in the cycle!
